answer: DeepWalk’s matrix factorization preserves community structure because the matrix it factorizes is built from random-walk co-occurrence statistics, so nodes that are often reached from each other within short walks get similar rows and therefore similar embeddings. In graph terms, random walks stay longer within densely connected regions than they do across sparse cuts, so the resulting co-occurrence matrix implicitly captures proximity and shared neighborhood context. When this matrix is factorized, nodes in the same community are pulled close together in the embedding space because they have similar walk-based context distributions. This is why DeepWalk tends to preserve community structure rather than just immediate edges: it encodes higher-order connectivity patterns from the graph’s random-walk dynamics.
